capacity_usable_kwh.notes: EV Database: 59 kWh usable of 62 kWh nominal (MY19-22 and MY23-25 pages agree); Wikipedia also says 59 kWh usable. Nissan USA marketing calls the 2023+ pack "60 kWh".

capacity_gross_kwh.notes: EV Database: nominal 62 kWh (MY23-25). The 2024 US and Canadian press kits print "60 kWh" for the SV PLUS (marketing figure).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 400 V architecture, nominal about 350 V (96S).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: EV Database states battery preconditioning is not supported (or "No") for this pack. Nissan US press kits (2012, 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2024) describe only remote cabin heating/cooling (NissanConnect EV) and, in 2012-2014, a cold-weather battery heater that warms the pack while charging; none describes a navigation or manual battery-warming-before-charging feature. Nissan's navigation-linked battery heater first appears on the third-generation LEAF.

dc_max_kw.notes: 2019 US press kit: LEAF PLUS has a "standard new 100kW capacity quick charging system". EV Database lists max DC 46 kW (10-80 % average 44 kW) for this pack and the 2019 kit itself gives 80 % in 45 min, so 100 kW is a brief peak at best. OWNER FLAG: Nissan figure kept as manufacturer. 2019 kit applied to this later year of the same pack (EV Database MY19-22 and MY23-25 pages show no change). Nissan Canada 2024 press kit also lists 100 kW for the SV PLUS.

ac_max_kw.notes: 2024 US press kit: 6.6 kW onboard charger (6.0 kW output) listed for all trims. Convention: the onboard-charger rating as Nissan prints it for that year (3.3 kW in the 2011-12 sheets; 3.6 kW rating / 3.3 kW output on later US S sheets; 6.6 kW rating / 6.0 kW output). Canada 2019 and 2024 sheets list 6.6 kW (6.0 kW output) too.
